title: Book Two · Chapter 28: The Narrow Bridge
story:
On Sunday afternoon, Leo comes to the green gate.

He has the folded white paper from his first reading-room meeting. The small bridge is on the front. He opens all three parts on the table.

“Can I look?” Ronan asks.

“That is why I brought it.”

Mum is going out to deliver a shirt. She asks the boys to leave her sewing basket on its shelf. They may use the clear half of the table.

Ronan sits beside Leo.

“Did you ask about the activity?” Leo asks.

“My parents are counting the cost.”

“Will you come?”

“I do not know yet. I want to.”

Leo nods. He pushes the open paper a little closer.

“We can read this now.”

Ronan reads the title: THE SMALL BRIDGE.

“I know bridge,” he says. “I asked Miss Wu about that word.”

“Read this bit.”

Leo points inside. Two lines have marks underneath. The word under has a circle round it.

The page tells a short story. A boy comes to a narrow bridge. Water runs under the bridge. A man is at the other end with a wide box. The boy waits. The man comes across first. Then the boy crosses.

Ronan reads the lines slowly. Leo puts his own finger beside the picture.

“Why does the boy wait?” Leo asks.

Ronan looks back at the words.

“The man comes across first.”

“Yes. But why?”

“Does he know the man?”

“The story does not say.”

They look at the picture together. The box reaches from one side of the bridge to the other. The boy stands on the road, away from it.

“There is no room for both,” Ronan says.

Leo puts his hand across the little bridge picture.

“Like this.”

Ronan uses one finger for the boy. Leo's hand blocks the way. There is no room for Ronan's finger on the bridge.

He stops. Then Leo moves his hand away. Ronan sends the little finger across.

“The box is wide,” he says. “The bridge is narrow.”

Leo nods. “I read narrow. I did not use that part in my answer.”

“Did the teacher tell you?”

“She asked me to look at the picture. Then she helped another child. I needed more time.”

Ronan looks at the two lines. He thought all the reading-room words would be easy for Leo.

“Was everything else easy?”

“No. There was another page yesterday. I did not finish the last question.”

“You went again yesterday?”

“Yes. We read a different story.”

Leo folds one edge back, then opens it again.

“I like the room. We can read quietly there. But some parts are hard.”

Ronan brings his bowl story. He tells Leo about the word after and the two wrong boxes.

“Jun made you read it again?”

“Yes.”

“Did you like that?”

“Not at first.”

Leo laughs. Then he reads the bowl line himself. He puts lunch before the return and moves his hands from left to right.

“Now your soup can stay for lunch.”

Ronan makes a face at him. They put their papers aside and draw a bridge across a scrap. Leo draws the wide box. Ronan adds a man with very short legs.

“He needs help with that box,” Leo says.

“He needs longer legs.”

They laugh. Leo must leave soon to meet his mother. He takes the folded page home. Ronan keeps their silly bridge picture and clears the table for Mum.
studyGuide:
## 重点表达

- narrow＝窄的
- across＝从一边到另一边
- deliver＝送交
- aside＝放在一旁

情节词：under＝在……下面（折页上圈出的词）；wide＝宽的。

## 理解问题

1. 图和narrow这个词怎样帮助两人解释男孩为什么等待？
2. Leo怎样描述课外活动的好处与仍然存在的困难？

## 从认词到读句子

正文原句：*The bridge is narrow.*

**The bridge / is / narrow.**

桥／是／窄的。这是完整的“对象＋状态”，不是说男孩不认识那个人。
